title: Garment workers block highway in Dhaka demanding wage hike and arrears

tea.why: Garment workers are protesting over unpaid wages, delayed arrears, and inadequate compensation.
tea.want: Demonstrators are demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000, payment of arrears, and other benefits.
tea.changed: Oct 15: Police used sound grenades and water cannons to disperse demonstrators blocking the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway in Uttara.

summary: Garment workers from several factories in Dhaka's Uttara area launched multi-day demonstrations to demand a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000, payment of outstanding arrears, and additional benefits. The protests involved blocking the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway, causing severe traffic congestion. Clashes broke out when police attempted to clear the road after protesters reportedly hurled brickbats at law enforcement officers. According to police statements, authorities responded by deploying water cannons and sound grenades to disperse the crowd after negotiations failed.
response: Police used sound grenades and water cannons to disperse the protesters, according to the Dhaka Metropolitan Police.

injuries.text: At least 17 police personnel were injured

updates.text: Apparel workers began demonstrating in Uttara to press demands for higher wages and arrears.
Workers continued staging protests for consecutive days, disrupting traffic on the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway.
